brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 4 November; new research covers 17:10 CET on 3 November to 05:10 CET on 4 November, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Drone Hits an Ozon Warehouse in Russia's Adygea Republic
items.lede: The online retailer said a fire broke out and staff were evacuated, with no injuries reported so far.

sections.text: A drone struck an Ozon logistics center in Russia's Adygea Republic overnight into 4 November, the company said in a statement reported by the Kyiv Independent [1]. Ozon said it evacuated all employees, no one was injured, and a fire broke out [1]. The company said goods in the warehouse were pulled from its online store [1]. Adygea's head, Murat Kumpilov, later said a drone attack caused a fire at the Ozon logistics center in Adygeysk and no casualties were reported, RIA Novosti reported [2]. No Ukrainian claim of responsibility was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Russian sources, the company and Adygea's head, relayed by the Kyiv Independent and Russian state media.

items.title: Ukraine Charges Zelensky's Former Spokeswoman Iuliia Mendel With Treason
items.lede: The SBU and prosecutors filed the charges in absentia, accusing the now-critic of spreading pro-Kremlin narratives under martial law.

sections.text: Ukraine's Security Service and the Prosecutor General's Office charged Iuliia Mendel with treason in absentia on 3 November, the Kyiv Independent reported [3]. The agencies accused her of "information and subversive activities against Ukraine" and of justifying Russia's war [3]. Mendel was Zelensky's press secretary from 2019 to 2021 and later became a vocal critic who called him a "dictator" [3]. In May she appeared on Tucker Carlson's podcast, and in September she spoke at an event hosted by Germany's AfD party [3]. Prosecutors said the case rests on her public statements, including the Carlson interview, and cited treason under martial law [4]. No response from Mendel was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the charges were filed, based on the Prosecutor General's Office statement and the Kyiv Independent; the allegations are unproven and the evidence is not public.

items.title: US Sets Ukraine-Russia Talks in Abu Dhabi for 10-11 November
items.lede: US envoy Steve Witkoff said Ukrainian and Russian delegations will meet in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, with Witkoff and Jared Kushner expected to represent Washington.

sections.text: US envoy Steve Witkoff said Monday that the United States will bring Ukrainian and Russian delegations together in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, Reuters reported [5]. He said the talks will cover post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures, and ending the war [5]. Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent the United States, a senior US official told Reuters [5]. US officials will also meet French, German, British, EU, and NATO representatives in Brussels this week on Ukraine's security guarantees, the official said [5]. Dutch broadcaster NOS also reported the Abu Dhabi talks early Tuesday [6]. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed Tuesday that a delegation led by Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky will take part, the Kyiv Independent reported [7]. The European Commission said it will host officials from Ukraine, the US, France, Germany, Britain, NATO, and the World Bank in Brussels on 4 November to prepare [8].

Confidence is moderate because the dates come only from the US side, which Witkoff announced on the record, as Reuters reported. The Kremlin confirmed Russia will take part, but neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed the dates by the cutoff.

items.title: Russian Bombs Kill at Least 33 at an Aid Center in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Region
items.lede: President Zelensky called it utterly horrific and said a second strike hit the place where people were sheltering after the first.

sections.text: At least 26 people were killed when Russian aerial bombs hit an aid distribution center in Komyshuvakha, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, on Monday [9]. Regional head Mykhailo Semikin said at least nine 3,000-kilogram bombs hit the village [9]. He said five people were injured and 27 were initially reported missing [9]. Zelensky said the first strike hit a local school used to hand out aid [9]. Ukraine's emergency service confirmed 24 deaths, including two rescuers and four police officers [9]. Zelensky raised the toll to 26 in his late Monday video address [9][10]. By Tuesday, at least 31 people had been killed and 48 were missing, acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said, the Kyiv Independent reported [11]. Semikin later put the toll at 33 dead, with 48 people missing [12]. Zelensky said more than 50 people could still be under the rubble [12][13]. Russia's Defense Ministry said the strike targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen, the BBC reported [13]. The BBC said it found no credible evidence of military use of the site [13].

Confidence is high on the strike and the toll, which BBC News and the Kyiv Independent attribute to Ukrainian officials. The toll rose to 33 on Tuesday and may still change. Russia's claim of a military target is unsupported.

items.title: Russia's Biggest Energy Strike of the Year Cuts Power Across Ukraine
items.lede: Russia's biggest attack on Ukraine's energy system this year hit 10 regions, the Kyiv Independent reported, and regional authorities counted 38 dead over the past day.

sections.text: Russia launched its biggest mass attack on Ukraine's energy facilities this year overnight into Tuesday, the Kyiv Independent reported [14]. Strikes hit substations, transmission lines, and power plants in 10 regions and cut power to households [14]. Ukrenergo chief Vitalii Zaichenko said it was one of the largest ballistic missile waves on critical infrastructure [14]. DTEK said generation stopped at three of its thermal power plants [14]. Ukraine's air force said Russia fired ballistic missiles, 59 cruise missiles, and 289 attack drones [11]. It said air defenses downed or jammed three ballistic missiles, 49 cruise missiles, and 257 drones [15]. A morning missile strike on Dnipro killed two people and injured 20, regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said [11]. Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov said a hospice was destroyed and about 50 patients were moved [11]. Regional authorities said Russian attacks killed at least 38 people and injured 167 over the past day [11]. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said strikes on the regional distribution network caused emergency power cuts and water outages in Kyiv [16]. City authorities suspended tram and trolleybus service from Tuesday evening and set up warming centers [16].
Confidence is high on the scale and damage, which the Kyiv Independent attributes to named Ukrainian officials and companies. Casualty totals are preliminary.

items.title: Overnight Russian Barrage Hits Infrastructure in Dnipro and a Kharkiv Hospital
items.lede: Kharkiv prosecutors said 73 people were hurt at a medical facility, and the mayor said about 200 patients were being moved to other hospitals.

sections.text: Russia launched a large combined missile and drone attack on Ukraine overnight into Tuesday, Glavcom reported, citing Ukraine's air force [17]. The air force warned of ballistic missiles heading toward the Dnipropetrovsk, Vinnytsia, and Kharkiv regions [17]. Explosions were reported in Khmelnytskyi, Rivne, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipro [17]. Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said Russia hit critical infrastructure in Dnipro and the Kryvyi Rih district [17]. Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov said 25 people were injured at a hospital [17]. Regional head Oleh Syniehubov said the strike hit a passage between hospital buildings in the Nemyshlianskyi district [17]. Terekhov had first reported four injured and heavy damage to the building, Interfax-Ukraine reported [18]. He said about 200 patients would be moved to other hospitals [17]. Residents of Zhytomyr reported power outages [17]. The Kharkiv regional prosecutor's office later put the number injured at the medical facility at 73 [19]. Terekhov said the strike damaged more than 1,000 windows [19].
Confidence is moderate. The first account came from one live blog, and a later Kyiv Independent report raised the Kharkiv injury count.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Norway Deploys Air Defense Sensors on Russian Border to Spot Stray Drones
items.lede: Troops in Kirkenes will watch for drones crossing from Russia, a move the defense minister called preventive.

sections.text: Norway's armed forces will place air surveillance sensors in Kirkenes, near the Russian border, to detect stray drones, NRK reported [1]. The sensors come from the NASAMS air defense system, The Barents Observer reported [2]. A team of 30 service members will operate them [2]. Defense Minister Tore O. Sandvik called the deployment a preventive measure [2]. "We have seen in other countries that drones can go astray," Sandvik said [2].
Confidence is high because NRK and The Barents Observer both report the deployment, citing Norway's Defense Ministry.

items.title: Poland Sends Counterterrorism Police Toward Kaliningrad After Sabotage Warnings
items.lede: Polish police chief Marek Boroń said the units are working with the army, border guards, and intelligence services in two northeastern regions.

sections.text: Poland deployed police counterterrorism units near Russia's Kaliningrad exclave after intelligence warnings of possible sabotage, the Kyiv Independent reported, citing RMF FM [3]. National police chief Marek Boroń said the units work with the military, border guards, and intelligence services in the Warmian-Masurian and Podlaskie regions [3]. A special command center was set up at national police headquarters [3]. Police headquarters told RMF FM the operation relates to sabotage and the actions of eastern services, Notes From Poland reported [4]. RMF FM said Polish and allied military intelligence warned last week of possible sabotage near the border, including incursions by armed groups [3]. Boroń denied any link to Poland's Constitutional Tribunal dispute [3].
Confidence is high on the deployment, which the police chief confirmed on the record, as several outlets reported. The intelligence warning rests on RMF FM's unnamed sources.

items.title: Bomb Threats Force Searches of Seven Passenger Jets Across Europe
items.lede: Airport sources in Rome said no explosives were found on two Ryanair flights searched there, and the Italian air force escorted the flight from Dublin.

sections.text: Seven passenger planes in Europe were searched Tuesday after a series of suspected bomb threats, BBC News reported [5]. Two of the flights had departed from the UK [5]. Two Ryanair flights, from Dublin and Lisbon, were searched after landing at Rome's Fiumicino airport, and no explosives were found, airport sources told the BBC [5]. The Italian air force escorted the Dublin flight until it landed [5]. Authorities also searched planes in Poland, Spain, and Bulgaria [5]. Officials in Spain and Bulgaria said no explosives were found either [5]. The UK government called the incidents malicious hoax threats [5]. The flight bound for Warsaw was diverted to the smaller Modlin airport, briefly forcing its closure, BBC News reported [5]. Officially there is no link between the incidents, but authorities in several countries are working together to assess whether they were coordinated, the BBC said [5]. No government has said who made the threats. In Greece, a bomb alert forced the evacuation of 1,537 passengers and crew from the Israel-bound cruise ship Crown Iris at Syros, and initial checks found no explosives [5].
Confidence is high that the searches took place, based on BBC reporting and NOS. Nothing is known about who made the threats.

items.title: Hackers Warm Supermarket Freezers in Belgium and Nine Other European Countries
items.lede: Belgian federal prosecutors opened a criminal case as stores threw out spoiled food, and no one had claimed responsibility by early Tuesday.

sections.text: A cyberattack early Monday hit fridges and freezers in dozens of European supermarkets [6]. AFP reported early Tuesday that stores in at least nine European countries were hit, including Italy and Portugal, forcing some to discard food [7]. No one had claimed responsibility, AFP said [7]. The BBC said Tuesday that supermarkets in 10 countries, including Germany, had reported problems [8]. About 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected [6]. Belgian refrigeration firm Sabcobel said units were switched to defrost mode, the method believed to have been used in an October attack in France [6]. A Belgian ethical hacker told VRT the attackers used a known flaw in Danfoss equipment [9]. Belgian federal prosecutors opened a criminal investigation [9][10]. EU Agriculture Commissioner Christophe Hansen called the attacks a deliberate attempt to disrupt the EU food supply [11]. Britain's National Cyber Security Centre said it knew of "a couple of instances" in the UK where vulnerable technology was exploited [12]. In Estonia, ERR reported that attackers reached the control computer of an older Danfoss refrigeration system at a Selver store [13].

Confidence is high on the attack, the countries hit, and the Belgian criminal case, which several major outlets report from official statements. The Danfoss flaw rests on one outside expert quoted by VRT.

theaters.heading: Politics, security, and defense across the EU and NATO's European members

items.title: Ireland's Prime Minister Plans an Initiative on the Island's Constitutional Future
items.lede: Micheál Martin's move comes as his coalition partner Fine Gael prepares its own blueprint on Irish unity.

sections.text: Ireland's Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, is to set up a new initiative on the constitutional future of the island of Ireland, BBC News reported [1]. The move comes as coalition partner Fine Gael is to unveil plans for its own blueprint [1]. Martin outlined the Futures Study Initiative to his Fianna Fáil lawmakers on Tuesday [1][2]. It will examine three scenarios, including a unitary republic and an all-island state with devolved government in Northern Ireland [1][2]. It will invite submissions from every party and publish a report to the government [1].
Confidence is high because BBC News and RTÉ both report the plan from Martin's policy paper to his party.

items.title: Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente Quits Over the Urda Rail Disaster
items.lede: He told Congress no minister could stay after two such crashes in under a year, and he will not run in the early election.

sections.text: Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente resigned on Tuesday, six days after a high-speed train collision near Urda killed at least 69 people, BBC News reported [3]. He announced the decision in Congress after testifying on the 28 October crash and outlining new rail safety measures [3]. Puente cited January's crash on the same line, which killed 46 people [3]. He also withdrew from his party's lists for the early legislative election [3]. The People's Party, Vox, and some government allies had called for him to go [3].
Confidence is high, based on BBC reporting of his statement in Congress.

items.title: Dutch Minority Cabinet Seeks Opposition Votes for Its Budget Plans
items.lede: Prime Minister Rob Jetten urged rival parties to take responsibility as his coalition, 10 seats short of a majority, faces a Wednesday debate.

sections.text: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten called on opposition parties to take responsibility for the Netherlands' budget, NOS reported [4]. Parliament debates the plans on Wednesday [5]. The centre-right coalition of D66, the VVD, and the CDA is 10 seats short of a majority in the lower house, DutchNews reported [5]. The latest budget includes about 350 million euros in sweeteners for opposition parties [5]. The coalition hopes to win support from the ChristenUnie, 50Plus, and Markuszower's group, which hold 11 seats between them [5].
Confidence is high because NOS and DutchNews both report Jetten's appeal and the coalition's search for votes.

items.title: Eurozone Opens the Race to Succeed Lagarde at the European Central Bank
items.lede: Governments using the euro have until Friday to nominate candidates for the top job in Frankfurt.

sections.text: The European Union has formally opened the process to replace European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, Euronews reported [6]. Eurogroup President Kyriakos Pierrakakis, Greece's finance minister, asked member states to send nominations by 6 November, a spokesperson said [6]. POLITICO Europe also reported the 6 November deadline [7]. Eurozone finance ministers will review the names at their meeting on 9 November [6]. A candidate needs the backing of at least 16 of the 21 eurozone countries, representing at least 65% of the bloc's population [6]. EU leaders then make the final appointment [6].
Confidence is high because Euronews and POLITICO Europe both report the nomination deadline, citing the Eurogroup.

items.title: Czech Public Broadcasters Strike Over Funding as Thousands Rally in Prague
items.lede: Thousands rallied in Prague as Czech Radio and Czech Television staff struck against a government plan to fund the broadcasters from the state budget.

sections.text: Czech Radio said Monday it will scale back news programs during a one-day staff strike on Tuesday [8]. Music, repeats, and archive shows will replace regular programs on several national and regional stations [8]. The broadcaster said it would keep basic news coverage and inform the public in an emergency [8]. Veřejnoprávně, a group representing Czech Radio and Czech Television employees, called the strike [8][9]. It opposes the governing coalition's plan to abolish license fees and fund both broadcasters from the state budget [8][9]. A group spokesman said the strike would affect all Czech Television channels, especially the news channel ČT24 [9]. Czech Television said its ČT24 news channel would switch to reduced programming at midnight, with a short news bulletin every hour [10]. Its main evening newscast and morning show will not air [10]. Thousands of people rallied on Prague's Wenceslas Square on Tuesday afternoon to back the broadcasters' independence, ČTK reported [11]. Several hundred striking Czech Television staff marched from its headquarters, and the procession grew to several thousand people [11]. Prime Minister Andrej Babiš rejected the strikers' arguments [11].
Confidence is high on the strike, its cause, and the rally, per Czech Radio's English service, ČT24, and ČTK. Both outlets belong to the striking broadcasters.

items.title: French Police Make Dozens of Arrests as School Blockades Spread
items.lede: Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said more than 1,300 police officers and gendarmes have been injured during the protest movement so far.

sections.text: France's Education Ministry said 48 of about 3,700 high schools were blocked at 9:30 a.m. Tuesday [12][13]. The student union USL claimed 500 [13]. The ministry said 51 higher-education sites were disrupted [12]. The Rhône prefecture reported 17 arrests linked to the blockades, including for firing fireworks and setting fires [13]. The Seine-Maritime prefecture reported 13 arrests by 2 p.m. [14]. It said three school principals were targeted with mortars or thrown objects, and one was slightly hurt [14]. Police arrested three students over the 1 October fire at a Nantes high school [12][13]. Authorities banned a rally in Rennes [13]. Darmanin said more than 1,300 police and gendarmes have been injured in the protests [12]. Paris police had banned a student march from the Panthéon to the Medef headquarters and offered a Porte de Charenton to Porte de Montreuil route instead [15]. A Paris administrative court rejected an emergency challenge to the ban without a hearing, police said [12]. Several hundred students marched in the Latin Quarter anyway, while the authorized Porte de Charenton start stayed nearly empty, Ouest-France reported [12]. A national protest day is set for Thursday, 5 November [13].
Confidence is moderate because the figures come from live blogs quoting ministries, prefectures, and police.

items.title: UK and EU Agree a Draft Deal to Remove Post-Brexit Food Checks
items.lede: Britain and the European Union settled a 200-page text on food and farm trade ahead of a 20 November summit.

sections.text: The United Kingdom and the EU have reached a draft deal to remove post-Brexit checks on food and farm exports, the BBC reported [16]. The 200-page text was circulated to EU governments for a meeting in Brussels on Wednesday [16][17]. Sources told The Guardian the text has been settled and will not be renegotiated [17]. The deal is not expected to take effect until early 2028 [17]. A change of UK prime minister delayed the second UK-EU summit by six months, to 20 November, The Guardian said [17]. Exports of fresh sausages, burgers, and seed potatoes could resume [16]. In return, Britain is expected to follow EU food and farm rules as they change [16]. The UK government says the deal will eventually add 5.1 billion pounds a year to the economy [16].
Confidence is high on the draft and its timing, which the BBC and The Guardian report from sources. The 5.1 billion pound figure is the UK government's estimate.

theaters.heading: Security, politics, and Russian pressure on Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania

items.title: Estonian and Lithuanian Troops Join First Drill of a Postwar Ukraine Force
items.lede: Estonia will send a company-sized unit to an exercise in Poland, the first drill of a French- and British-led force meant for Ukraine after the fighting ends.

sections.text: The Estonian Defense Forces will send a company-sized unit to Exercise Koalicja in Poland, ERR News reported [1]. The Multinational Force Ukraine, led by France and the UK, runs the drill [1]. About 2,800 troops from 10 European countries, including Estonia and Lithuania, will train from 9 to 22 November, Euronews reported [2]. They will operate around Nowa Dęba, about 100 kilometers west of the Ukrainian border [2]. France will send the largest contingent, 1,100 troops, and the UK will send 300 [2]. The force is not a NATO operation and would deploy only after a ceasefire [2].
Confidence is high because ERR News and Euronews both report the drill, citing the Estonian military and a French and British joint statement.

items.title: Latvian Troops Search for a Drone After an Overnight Air Alert Near Russia
items.lede: Latvia's military said the drone probably crashed in the Balvi district, but its type and origin have not been confirmed.

sections.text: Latvia's armed forces declared an air threat in the Balvi and Ludza districts at 23:10 CET Monday and lifted it at 23:35 CET, LSM reported [3]. Two military interceptor drones were launched to find and identify the aircraft [3]. NATO fighter jets on the Baltic Air Policing mission were also scrambled [3][4]. The military said the drone looked similar to those used by Ukraine's armed forces, but its type and origin were not confirmed [3]. National Guard units were searching for it in the Balvi district, where it may have crashed [3]. The head of the Balvi council told the LETA news agency the object may have fallen near Tilža [4]. On Sunday, Latvia blew up its own interceptor drone at the border after chasing a drone it judged most likely a Russian Geran [3].
Confidence is high on the alert and the search, which the military described at a briefing reported by LSM and LETA. The drone's origin is unconfirmed.

items.title: Latvia's New Parliament Elects Edvards Smiltēns Speaker Again
items.lede: The United List politician returns to the post he held from 2022 to 2023, winning 79 of the Saeima's 100 votes.

sections.text: Latvia's 15th Saeima, the national parliament, elected Edvards Smiltēns of the United List as its speaker Tuesday, the parliament said [5]. He won 79 votes, while 15 deputies backed his rival, Julija Stepaņenko, LSM reported [6]. Smiltēns led the previous parliament from 2022 to 2023 and has served as justice minister in Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' government [5][7]. He replaces Daiga Mieriņa of the Union of Greens and Farmers, whose party won no seats in the 3 October election [6]. The speaker represents parliament abroad and stands in for the president when the head of state is out of the country [6]. Six deputies spoiled their ballots, LSM reported [6].
Confidence is high because the parliament's press service, Latvian public media, and the LETA news agency all report the result.

items.title: Lithuania Bars In-Country Work and Study Permit Requests From Schengen Visa Holders
items.lede: Most such applicants must now apply through VFS Global centers abroad, though highly qualified workers are exempt.

sections.text: Since 1 November, some foreigners can no longer apply for Lithuanian temporary residence permits for work or undergraduate study while inside the country, LRT reported [8]. The rule covers people who entered on Schengen visas or on national visas issued by other countries [8]. In-country applications are now limited to holders of Lithuanian permits or visas, other EU or Schengen permits, or visa-free entry [8]. Others must apply through VFS Global centers abroad [8]. Highly qualified workers are exempt, the Migration Department said [8].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on LRT citing BNS and the Migration Department.

items.title: Lithuania's Nausėda Says Some Russian Attacks Are Kinetic, Not Hybrid
items.lede: He spoke as he opened the Berlin Security Conference, which Germany is co-hosting with Lithuania.

sections.text: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Tuesday the term hybrid threats has become a convenient euphemism, LRT reported [9]. He said it lets people avoid saying plainly what Europe is experiencing from Russia [9]. Nausėda said some recent attacks are in essence kinetic attacks [9]. He spoke in a statement as he opened the Berlin Security Conference, co-hosted by Germany and Lithuania [9]. He said greater European responsibility for defense should strengthen NATO [9].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on LRT citing the president's office; the statement itself was not read.

theaters.heading: Stability, politics, and outside influence in the Western Balkans

items.title: Europol Raids in Albania, Kosovo, and North Macedonia Net Seven Fraud Suspects
items.lede: Eurojust said more than 100 servers were shut down, and Germany is weighing extradition of those arrested.

sections.text: Eurojust said Tuesday that seven people were arrested in an action against an investment fraud network, Balkan Insight reported [1]. The operation also involved Germany, Cyprus, Finland, Albania, Kosovo, North Macedonia, and Israel [1]. Eurojust said more than 100 servers were shut down [1]. Germany's Itzehoe prosecutor's office led the case, Europol said [1]. It targeted a company suspected of supplying fake trading websites to call centers that persuaded victims to hand over savings [1].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Balkan Insight quoting Eurojust and Europol; their releases were not read.

items.title: EU Draft Plan Puts Montenegro on Track to Sign an Accession Treaty in June 2027
items.lede: A leaked European Commission plan, due out Wednesday, would have Montenegro close its remaining EU negotiating chapters by the end of this year.

sections.text: Radio Free Europe obtained a draft European Commission plan for Montenegro's EU accession, Albania's CNA reported [2]. Croatia's Jutarnji list said it also obtained the draft, which commissioners are due to adopt Wednesday [3]. Under the plan, Montenegro would close its remaining chapters at conferences in November and December [2][3]. Work on the accession treaty would finish in spring 2027, and the treaty could be signed in June 2027 [2][3]. Montenegro has provisionally closed 21 of 33 chapters [2]. The Commission said the dates are not final and depend on Montenegro meeting the conditions [2]. The plan is part of roadmaps for Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine, and Moldova [2].
Confidence is moderate because both reports rest on the same leaked draft. Wednesday's adoption would confirm it.

items.title: Serbian Court Jails Two Senior Police Chiefs for 30 Days Pending Trial
items.lede: The criminal police director also faces a torture charge linked to a May killing in a Belgrade restaurant.

sections.text: Serbia's Higher Court in Belgrade on Tuesday ordered 30 days' detention for criminal police director Marko Kricak and crime suppression chief Bosko Sekulovic, Balkan Insight reported [4]. Both are charged with abuse of office, and Kricak also with mistreatment and torture [4]. The charges are linked to their handling of a 12 May killing in a Belgrade restaurant [4]. The court said detention was needed to keep them from influencing witnesses [4]. Prosecutors said they would appeal, arguing the two could also reoffend [4]. The two were arrested Sunday, a week after elections ended the Serbian Progressive Party's 14-year rule [4]. Belgrade's chief prosecutor said the arrests have nothing to do with the election [4].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Balkan Insight alone.

items.title: Bosnia's State Court Sentences Six Ex-Soldiers for 1992 Crimes Near Sokolac
items.lede: The six former Bosnian Serb brigade members received 83 years in total, with the longest term set at 20 years.

sections.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina's state court sentenced six former members of the Second Romanija Brigade to a combined 83 years for crimes against humanity, Balkan Insight reported [5]. The crimes took place near Sokolac in eastern Bosnia in 1992 [5]. Momcilo Pajic got 20 years and Miladin Gasevic 15 [5]. Four others got 12 years each [5]. The court found the aim of the action in Novoseoci village was the ethnic cleansing of Bosniak residents [5]. The court acquitted two other defendants, Dragomir Obradovic and Aleksa Gordic [5].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Balkan Insight's court report alone.

items.title: Jailed Tirana Mayor Accuses Albania's Rama of Pressuring Him to Resign
items.lede: Justice Minister Toni Gogu confirmed visiting Erion Veliaj in prison but denied carrying any messages from the prime minister.

sections.text: Jailed Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj said Monday that Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama used a minister to press him to resign, Balkan Insight reported [6]. Veliaj's lawyer said Justice Minister Toni Gogu brought Rama's demands to the prison on Friday [6]. Veliaj said he was asked to admit he stands behind the recent violent protests in Tirana [6]. Gogu confirmed the meeting but denied passing on any such messages [6]. Veliaj later posted two handwritten notes he said came from the meeting [6].
Confidence is moderate on the competing claims, which rest on Balkan Insight; neither side's account has been independently confirmed.

items.title: Serbian Prosecutors Detain Alta Bank Owner Over Cash Taken From Its Vault
items.lede: Prosecutors say Davor Macura took about 45 billion dinars from the vault of the bank, whose license Serbia's central bank revoked on Saturday.

sections.text: Serbia's Organized Crime Prosecutor's Office said Monday it had detained Alta Bank's owner and two bank employees, B92 reported [7]. AP named the owner as Davor Macura [8]. Prosecutors said the two employees gave him access to the bank's vault, where he allegedly removed cash [7]. They put the illegal gain at about 45 billion dinars, which AP put at about $428 million [7][8]. The suspects were ordered held for 48 hours [7]. Serbia's central bank revoked Alta Bank's license on Saturday and started bankruptcy proceedings, AP reported [8]. The bank rose under President Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party, which lost the 25 October election, AP said [8]. It handled Belgrade's electricity and public parking payments [8]. Macura's lawyers said he cooperated with the police search [8].
Confidence is high because the prosecutors' statement and AP both report the detention. The charges are allegations, and Macura has not been charged in court.

items.title: Georgian Premier Kobakhidze Rejects EU Criticism at a Brussels Summit
items.lede: He defended the ruling party's bid to ban five opposition parties and challenged the European Commission to a debate a day before its enlargement reports.

sections.text: Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze dismissed European criticism of Georgia's democratic record in an interview at Euronews' EU Enlargement Summit in Brussels on 3 November, Civil Georgia reported [1]. He invited European Commission officials to a "debate" and said Georgia still wants to join the EU "with dignity" [1]. He defended Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban five opposition parties [1]. The event came a day before the Commission's annual enlargement reports, including one on Georgia [1]. Euronews, which conducted the interview, published its own report of the remarks [2].
Confidence is high because Civil Georgia and Euronews, which conducted the interview, report the same remarks.

items.title: Ivanishvili's Son Sues Two Georgian Opposition TV Channels
items.lede: Bera Ivanishvili wants TV Pirveli and Formula to retract reports that he protected scam call centers.

sections.text: Bera Ivanishvili, son of Georgian Dream founder Bidzina Ivanishvili, has sued Georgia's opposition-leaning TV Pirveli and Formula channels, Civil Georgia reported [3]. He demands that they retract reports about him that he calls defamatory [3]. The reports accused him of protecting scam call centers [3]. Civil Georgia cited the Georgian Public Broadcaster [3].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Civil Georgia citing the public broadcaster.

items.title: Azerbaijan Brings Home 11 Fraud Suspects Detained in Ukraine
items.lede: Four of them are accused of organizing call centers in Ukrainian cities that targeted Azerbaijani citizens, the Interior Ministry said.

sections.text: Azerbaijan returned 11 of its citizens detained in Ukraine in a joint operation against a cyberfraud network, OC Media reported [4]. Azerbaijan's Interior Ministry said four are alleged organizers who were on an international wanted list [4]. The network allegedly posed as bank officials, police, and investment firms to trick victims [4]. It ran illegal call centers in several Ukrainian cities [4].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on OC Media citing Azerbaijan's Interior Ministry.

items.title: Georgian Dream Attacks RSF for Naming Ivanishvili a Press Freedom Predator
items.lede: Reporters Without Borders listed the ruling party's founder for the second year in a row.

sections.text: Georgian Dream majority leader Irakli Kirtskhalia accused Reporters Without Borders of serving the deep state and a global war party, Civil Georgia reported [5]. He spoke at a briefing Tuesday [5]. The Paris-based group had put party founder Bidzina Ivanishvili on its press freedom predators list for a second straight year [5].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Civil Georgia alone.

items.title: Armenia Will Start Design Work on the Trump Route's Rail and Road Links
items.lede: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Armenia will hand the work to the TRIPP Development Company once it is set up.

sections.text: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Armenia will commission design work for the railway, highway, and power lines of the Trump Route, OC Media reported [6]. He said the aim is to avoid delays [6]. He said Armenia will hand the completed work to the TRIPP Development Company once it is set up [6]. He spoke during a budget debate in parliament on Monday [6]. The route would link Azerbaijan to its Nakhchivan exclave through Armenian territory [6]. Armenia, Azerbaijan, and the United States agreed to it in Washington in August 2025 [6].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on OC Media alone.

items.title: Georgia's UNM Party Leaves the Opposition Alliance After Months of Infighting
items.lede: The alliance had dropped the party from its Facebook logo a day earlier, before the UNM confirmed the split.

sections.text: Georgia's United National Movement has left the Opposition Alliance, a group of nine opposition forces formed in March, Civil Georgia reported [7]. The party's press service confirmed the exit on Tuesday after months of disagreements [7]. It did not say when the split became official [7]. The alliance removed the UNM from its Facebook logo on Monday [7].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on Civil Georgia's confirmation from the party.

items.title: Draft Report Projects a 4.1% Rise in German Pensions in 2027
items.lede: A pension of 1,000 euros would rise by 41 euros a month, though final figures are due only in March.

sections.text: Germany's government expects statutory pensions to rise 4.1% in 2027, according to a draft pension insurance report seen by ARD, tagesschau.de reported [1]. A pension of 1,000 euros would rise by 41 euros a month [1]. Last year's increase was 4.2% [1]. The estimate is preliminary, and exact data are due in March [1]. The contribution rate is set to stay at 18.6% next year and reach 20% by 2030 [1].
Confidence is high on the draft's figures as reported by the public broadcaster; the estimate itself is preliminary.

items.title: Hackers Switch German Supermarket Coolers to Heating in Three States
items.lede: Stores in North Rhine-Westphalia, Lower Saxony, and Bavaria had to throw out large amounts of food after the overnight attacks.

sections.text: Hackers switched refrigeration systems from cooling to heating overnight at several supermarkets in Germany, tagesschau.de reported [2]. Affected stores included two CAP markets in Wuppertal and Wetter, a Rewe in Raesfeld, and Edeka stores in Lilienthal and Reisbach [2]. The CAP operator told the dpa news agency that the attack targeted the company that remotely maintains the systems [2]. Large amounts of food had to be thrown out [2]. Similar attacks hit supermarkets in other European countries [2].
Confidence is high, based on public-broadcaster reporting with named stores and an operator's confirmation to dpa.

items.title: Germany Plans 200 Million Euros in Extra Winter Aid as Zelensky Visits Berlin
items.lede: Chancellor Merz said Germany will keep helping Ukraine until the war ends and urged other Europeans to carry their share.

sections.text: Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised Ukraine more help before winter after meeting President Volodymyr Zelensky in Berlin on Tuesday, tagesschau reported [3]. The extra winter aid is to total 200 million euros, according to the dpa news agency [3]. Half is to come from the Foreign Office budget and half from development funds, dpa said [3]. The governing coalition plans to seek parliament's approval for the money, citing power plants and other civilian infrastructure, Welt reported [4]. Merz said Germany is helping Ukraine in its own interest [3]. He said NATO allies agreed on 70 billion euros in military support for Ukraine in 2026, and that all partners must meet that pledge [3]. Zelensky also met Bundestag President Julia Klöckner, the Kyiv Post reported [5].
Confidence is moderate because the aid figure comes from dpa and government sources cited by Welt; no government release was read.

items.title: Turkey Frees Ulm Man Ferdi Soylu but Bars Him From Leaving the Country
items.lede: Soylu, a German citizen jailed in Ankara since August, was freed Monday evening but may not leave Turkey for now, his brother told dpa.

sections.text: Ferdi Soylu of Ulm, in the German state of Baden-Württemberg, was released from pretrial detention in Turkey on Monday evening, his brother Sebahattin Soylu told dpa, Der Spiegel reported [6]. He had been held in Ankara since August [7]. His lawyer says he is accused of membership in a terrorist organization [6]. He may not leave Turkey for now, and the family plans to challenge the ban [6]. No indictment or trial date has been set, his brother said [6]. SWR first reported the release [8].
Confidence is moderate because the account of the release comes from the family, as reported by dpa and SWR; no Turkish statement was found.

items.title: Schaeffler to Close Four German Sites and Cut 3,460 Jobs Worldwide
items.lede: The car parts maker said 2,660 of the jobs will go in Germany, saving 300 million euros a year from 2030.

sections.text: German auto and industrial supplier Schaeffler said Tuesday it will close four sites in Germany and cut 3,460 jobs worldwide, tagesschau reported [9]. Of those, 2,660 jobs are in Germany [9]. The company expects savings of 300 million euros a year from 2030 [9]. It cited a tough auto market and high labor costs in Germany [9]. Plants in Dortmund and Morbach that make combustion-engine parts will close, as will offices in Berlin and Schwalbach [9]. Schaeffler also wants staff to accept pay cuts, which it must still negotiate with the union [9].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on tagesschau's report of the company statement.

items.title: Germany Awards Subsidies for 11 Backup Power Plants to RWE, LEAG, and Karlsruhe
items.lede: The support totals about 12 billion euros over 15 years, and electricity customers will pay for it through a levy.

sections.text: Germany's Federal Network Agency awarded 11 contracts for about 5,160 megawatts of new backup power plants, tagesschau reported [10]. RWE and the lignite company LEAG won 10 of them [10]. Stadtwerke Karlsruhe won the other [10]. The plants are to secure supply from November 2031 when other sources fall short [10]. Operators get payments for 15 years, about 12 billion euros in total, paid by customers through a levy [10]. The tender drew 41 bids for nearly 12,000 megawatts against 4,500 offered [10].
Confidence is moderate because the account rests on tagesschau's report of the agency's announcement.
